title: Model circuit-breaker hysteresis and synthetic canary litmus: follow-up actions and runbook updates
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Follow-up work after a failed canary rollout where auto-rollback fired repeatedly and caused thrashing. Primary goal: reduce noisy rollbacks by introducing hysteresis into circuit-breakers, adding synthetic litmus tests to shadow traffic, and improving telemetry/alerting so operators can distinguish model quality regressions from transient infra noise.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-08 a staged model rollout for v2.11 triggered automated rollback three times over a 2-hour window. Symptoms included elevated 95th latency, increased short-lived 5xx spikes, and drift in token-level perplexity on a small set of customer-similar queries. The autoscaler and circuit-breaker rules interpreted transient KV cache warmup and batching backpressure as persistent degradation, causing rollout hysteresis to flip aggressively.
root_cause_analysis: Auto-rollback predicates relied on short-window P95 latency and error-rate only; no smoothing (hysteresis) or weighted-lead indicators were used.

Shadow traffic evaluation lacked synthetic litmus queries that exercise large-sequence KV cache reuse patterns; real customer queries warmed cache slowly causing initial latency which was mistaken for regression.
Batching backpressure under FIFO queueing produced spikes when small bursts of long-context requests entered the cohort; runtime did not tag or surface 'long seq' bursts to the rollout controller.

Telemetry contract mismatch: rollout controller consumed raw counters without percentiles that excluded cold-start artefacts; alerts had low signal-to-noise and not tied to model-quality metrics (perplexity/ROUGE proxies).
actions_taken: Immediately paused all active staged rollouts and opened incident bridge (Ops handled traffic steering to stable pool).
Manually stabilized production by pinning traffic to previous model version and clearing KV cache entries for affected pods to remove warmup noise.
Short-term fix: increased auto-rollback evaluation window from 60s to 5m and added a 2-minute stabilization delay before any automatic rollback can happen.
Deployed a hotfix to tag requests with 'seq_len' and 'synthetic' flags so the rollout controller can filter/weight signals.
runbook_updates: Add explicit triage steps for staged rollout failures that check KV cache warmup metrics, batch queue depth, and seq_len distribution before triggering rollback.

Introduce operator checklist: 1) identify whether latency spike aligns with cache rewarm or increased long-context traffic; 2) verify model-output-quality metrics (perplexity/semantic-embedding drift) before rollback; 3) if infra, flush cache and increase graceful-backoff; 4) if model, proceed to rollback.
Documented 'grace window' configuration recommendations per customer tier: Hosted=3m, Dedicated=2m, Private=5m (configurable).
Add runbook appendix with commands to: inspect KV cache heatmap, force cache flush, label pods for draining, and re-warm using synthetic litmus traffic.
telemetry_changes: Add a new-derived metric: p95_no_coldstart which excludes requests with 'pod_uptime < 2m' and 'seq_len > 2048'.
Publish seq_len-distribution dashboards alongside rollout dashboards and expose top-10 request exemplars for failed canary cohorts.
Rollout controller now consumes weighted signals: model-quality (50%), stable-latency (30%), error-rate (20%); also applies exponential smoothing with alpha=0.2.
Create an alert that triggers only if p95_no_coldstart and model-quality both degrade for longer than the grace window.
synthetic_tests: Create a set of 120 synthetic litmus queries that mimic long-context customer workloads and KV-cache-reuse patterns.

Add end-to-end synthetic canary: run litmus set against candidate model in shadow mode and require no >10% regression in median latency and no drift >0.8 perplexity units for 10 consecutive minutes before allowing traffic split.
Schedule nightly litmus runs against the model catalog for regression detection and surface trend alerts to the model-onboarding dashboard.
follow_ups: Implement hysteresis config in the rollout controller with tunable 'open' and 'close' thresholds to prevent flip-flop behavior (owner: Marcus Li, ETA: 2026-03-18).
Prototype a 'cache-warm probe' that prewarms KV cache in shadow before traffic shift; experiment in dedicated pools (owner: Priya Natarajan, ETA: 2026-03-25).

Run an A/B test comparing current rollback policy vs. hysteresis-enabled policy on internal canary traffic to quantify false-positive rollback rate reduction (owner: Data Reliability Team, ETA: 2026-04-01).
Coordinate with Console team to expose seq_len and p95_no_coldstart metrics in the rollout UI (owner: Console PM Sofia Ruiz, ETA: 2026-03-30).
comments: 2026-03-10 Marcus Li: Initial incident triage completed. Confirmed KV cache warmup aligned with first latency spike. Pinning traffic and flushing caches stabilized the surface-level symptoms.
2026-03-11 Priya Natarajan: Prototype for prewarm probe is ready; needs integration with shadow runner. Early results look promising in dedicated dev pool.
2026-03-12 Sofia Ruiz (Console PM): UX ticket opened to surface seq_len histograms; will align on layout in next design sync.
2026-03-12 Aisha Kapoor: Moving hysteresis change to 'In Review' for design and safety validation. Added test matrix for A/B comparison to detect regressions in rollback sensitivity.
